scenario: A space-technology newsletter features only observatory missions that survive deployment and maintain system uptime above 98%. Readers use the featured average uptime to estimate typical uptime across all missions.

data.description: Only surviving missions with uptime above 98% are featured. Uptime is Normal with sigma 1.5 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean uptime mu across all missions and (b) the fraction of missions featured.
naive_answer: Typical uptime is about 98.8% because that is the newsletter average.
naive_trap: The newsletter includes only high-uptime surviving missions.
reasoning_trace: Use the lower-truncated normal model with alpha around 1.1.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu):
    a=(98-mu)/1.5
    return mu+1.5*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-98.76
mu=brentq(eq,90,97.99)
frac=norm.sf((98-mu)/1.5)
assert abs(mu-96.35)<0.2 and abs(frac-0.1357)<0.005
